newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOUR KILLED AS BELGIAN COACH CRASHES IN BELARUS.
newsitem.headline: FOUR KILLED AS BELGIAN COACH CRASHES IN BELARUS.

text.p: Three young children from areas of Belarus affected by the Chernobyl nuclear accident and a Russian teenager were killed when their Belgian coach overturned on a wet Belarussian road, the company operating the vehicle said on Wednesday.

The dead were part of a group of more than 300 children travelling to Belgian hospitals in a convoy of four coaches, all from Belgium's Excelsior company. Sixty-three children were injured, three of them seriously.
The driver of the crashed coach was unhurt, Excelsior director Joseph Cannaerts told Reuters.
"The driver explained...he couldn't avoid a car and the bus overturned. It is seriously damaged, lying near the road," said Cannaerts.
The crash occurred near the Belarus village of Kobrin in wet conditions on Tuesday and after a car skidded in front of the double-decker coach, a Belgian Foreign Ministry spokesman said.
The 70 children on the crashed coach were aged between seven and 14.
Cannaerts said the 16-year-old Russian who was killed was possibly a translator.
The three seriously injured children were taken to a clinic near Kobrin.
The other three coaches would continue their journey on Wednesday afternoon and were expected to arrive in Belgium late on Thursday, Cannaerts said.
The children were invited to Belgium by a Flemish humanitarian association.
The accident at Chernobyl in Ukraine in April 1986 sent a radiation cloud over Belarus and other countries.
Many countries have been taking children from affected regions to hospitals and rehabilitation centres abroad for medical treatment.
